introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper. Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D.
incertitudes: Q3 : le sujet imprime « 1500. » sans unité dans la première phrase puis « 1000frs » ; recopié tel quel.

Q11 « car nuit à la santé » (sujet omis), Q12 « sur bulletins de vote » (article omis), Q20 « être de citoyens », Q22 « a organisé campagne de salubrité » (article omis) : imprimés ainsi, recopiés tels quels.
Scan photocopié avec filigrane : accents et élisions relus sur un rendu à 200 dpi, aucune zone illisible. Les blancs imprimés « ------ » sont écrits « ____ » ; apostrophes typographiques.

Clés défendables par deux options : Q32 (a broutent / b broute), Q48 (a proverbe exact / b paraphrase), Q49 (c Speed up to town / a Sit on their bikes), Q25 (d a eu lieu / a a pris place, calque de l'anglais), Q13 (d grammes / b hectogrammes, grammaticalement possible).
Q43 est une question de traduction (anglais vers français) glissée parmi les questions de grammaire ; thème « translation into French ».

questions.enonce_markdown: Mes enfants boivent ____ bouillie tous les matins avant d’aller à l’école.
questions.corrige_markdown: The verb "boire" takes a partitive article for an unspecified quantity. "Bouillie" is feminine and begins with a consonant, so the partitive is "de la". "Du" is masculine, "de l'" is used before a vowel, and "la" alone has no partitive sense. Rule: partitive = de + definite article (du, de la, de l', des). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Ma mère est ____ à l’hôpital régional.
questions.corrige_markdown: The sentence names a profession and the subject "ma mère" is a woman, so the feminine form "infirmière" (nurse) is needed. "Infirmier" is the masculine form, "infirmer" is a verb (to invalidate) and "infirme" means disabled. Rule: professions agree in gender with the person. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Cette vendeuse vend les tomates à 1500. Les autres les vendent à 1000frs. Alors, cette vendeuse est ____ du marché.
questions.corrige_markdown: She sells at 1500 while the others sell at 1000, so she is the most expensive seller. A superlative of superiority is "le/la/les plus + adjective", and the article and adjective agree with "vendeuse" (feminine singular): "la plus chère". "La moins chère" has the opposite meaning, and "le plus cher" and "les plus chers" are masculine or plural. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Mes camarades de classe ne ____ jamais en retard à l’école.
questions.corrige_markdown: The subject "mes camarades de classe" is third person plural, so the present of "venir" is "viennent". "Viens" goes with tu/je, "venons" with nous and "vient" with a singular subject. Rule: the verb agrees with its subject (ils/elles: -ent). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Cette dame a passé sa commande depuis ____ mai.
questions.corrige_markdown: Dates take the definite article and the cardinal number, except for the first day of the month, which takes the ordinal: "le premier mai". After "depuis" the article "le" stays. "La première" would be feminine (mai is masculine), and "en premier" and "au premier" are not used for dates. Rule: "le premier" + month, but "le deux", "le trois"... **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - numbers and fractions

questions.enonce_markdown: J’ai mal au pied donc je ne peux pas marcher ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: With a sore foot the person cannot walk quickly, so the fitting adverb is "doucement" (slowly). "Vite" and "rapide" would say the opposite (and "rapide" is an adjective), and "lent" is an adjective, not an adverb of manner. Rule: after a verb, use an adverb (doucement), not an adjective. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Les élèves absentéistes ____ peuvent ____ réussir à l’examen.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Les élèves absentéistes ne peuvent jamais réussir à l'examen" is correct: "ne ... jamais" surrounds the conjugated verb. "Ne ... personne" and "ne ... rien" need a person or a thing as object, and "ne ... ni" needs two coordinated elements (ne ... ni ... ni ...). Rule: "ne ... jamais" = never, placed around the conjugated verb. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: ____ école abrite un grand centre multimédia.
questions.corrige_markdown: "École" is feminine but begins with a vowel, so the possessive takes the masculine form "mon" to avoid a clash of vowels: "mon école". "Ma" and "ta" are not allowed before a vowel, and "m'a" is the pronoun m' plus the verb "a". Rule: mon/ton/son replace ma/ta/sa before a feminine noun starting with a vowel. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Les électeurs ____ déjà dans les bureaux de vote.
questions.corrige_markdown: The subject "les électeurs" is third person plural, so "arrivent". "Arrive" is singular, "arrives" is for tu and "arrivez" for vous. Rule: the verb agrees with its subject (ils/elles: -ent). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: ____ dix ans qu’il exerce ce métier de maçon.
questions.corrige_markdown: To say how long something has been going on, French uses "Il y a ... que" + present: "Il y a dix ans qu'il exerce ce métier". The main verb "exerce" is in the present, so "il y avait" and "c'était" (imperfect) do not fit, and "c'est" cannot introduce a duration this way. Rule: "il y a + duration + que + present". **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Ne prenez pas ____ de sucreries car nuit à la santé.
questions.corrige_markdown: Sweets harm health when taken in excess, so "ne prenez pas trop de sucreries" (do not take too many). "Très" and "bien" cannot be followed by "de" + noun, and "assez de" (enough) would make no sense as a warning. Rule: quantity adverbs take "de" (trop de, beaucoup de, assez de); "très" modifies adjectives and adverbs only. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Il y a les noms de ____ femmes sur bulletins de vote.
questions.corrige_markdown: Here we need the plural indefinite adjective meaning "a few": "quelques femmes". "Quelle(s) que" is a concessive form always followed by a subjunctive verb (quelles que soient...), and "quelque" alone is singular. Rule: "quelques" + plural noun = some, a few. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Dans cette recette de gâteau, j’ai mis dix-____ de beurre.
questions.corrige_markdown: Butter is measured by weight, so only "grammes" (and, in theory, hectogrammes) can fit; litres and kilomètres measure volume and distance. "Dix grammes" is the standard cooking unit; ten hectograms would be a whole kilogram of butter, which is unrealistic for one cake. Rule: choose the unit that matches the quantity measured (weight: grammes). **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - numbers and fractions

questions.enonce_markdown: Pendant la saison sèche, il fait très ____ dans ma région.
questions.corrige_markdown: In weather expressions with "il fait", the word after it is an invariable adjective: "il fait très chaud". "Chaleur" is a noun (it would need "il fait une grande chaleur"), "chaude" is feminine and "chauffe" is a verb form. Rule: "il fait + adjective" (chaud, froid, beau), always masculine singular. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Mon grand frère ____ 20 ans le mois prochain.
questions.corrige_markdown: French uses "avoir" to give age, and "le mois prochain" calls for the future: third person singular "aura". "Auras" and "aurai" do not match "mon grand frère", and "sera" is the future of être, wrong for expressing age. Rule: age is expressed with avoir (il aura 20 ans). **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Il ne faut jamais ____ ton mot de passe à qui que ce soit.
questions.corrige_markdown: After the impersonal "il faut", the verb is in the infinitive: "il ne faut jamais donner". The participle "donné" and the conjugated forms "donnez" and "donnes" cannot follow it. Rule: il faut + infinitive. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Après les pluies torrentielles d’hier beaucoup de maisons sont inondées mais ____ ne l’est pas.
questions.corrige_markdown: The possessive pronoun stands for "la maison" of the speaker's family, which is feminine singular: "la nôtre". "Les nôtres" is plural (and the verb "est" is singular), "le nôtre" is masculine, and "le vôtre" changes the owner. Rule: a possessive pronoun agrees in gender and number with the noun it replaces. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Ma mère n’est pas allée ____ champ ce matin parce qu’elle est malade.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Champ" is masculine singular, so "à" + "le" contracts to "au": "au champ". "Aux" is plural, "à la" is feminine and "à l'" is used before a vowel. Rule: à + le = au; à + les = aux. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Quand reviendras-tu du village ? ____ lundi.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Revenir du village" means to come back from the village, and the pronoun "en" replaces a complement introduced by "de" that expresses origin: "J'en reviendrai lundi". "Y" would replace a place of destination (à), "le" replaces a direct object, and "reviendrais" is a conditional while the question asks about the future. Rule: en = de + place or thing; y = à/dans + place. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Nous étudions ____ être de citoyens.
questions.corrige_markdown: Studying with the aim of becoming citizens needs a conjunction of purpose: "afin d'être". "De suite" means immediately, "avant d'" is time, and "à force d'" expresses repetition as a cause (à force d'étudier). Rule: afin de + infinitive = in order to. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: « Qui aime bien châtie bien. » Veut dire :
questions.corrige_markdown: The proverb means that real affection includes correcting a loved one when needed: "châtier" is to punish, so the idea is to punish in order to reform. "Chat" and "chatouiller" are wordplay traps based on sound, and option D reduces the proverb to a taste for punishing. Rule: "qui aime bien châtie bien" = love sometimes requires discipline. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Le ____ de la ville a organisé campagne de salubrité le weekend passé.
questions.corrige_markdown: The head of a town council is "le maire". "Mère" (mother), "mer" (sea) and "met" (puts) are homophones that do not fit after "le" in this sense. Rule: do not confuse the homophones maire, mère, mer. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Quand j’____ les moutons, je les ramènerai au marché.
questions.corrige_markdown: The main verb is in the simple future ("je ramènerai"), and the first action will be finished before the second, so the subordinate verb takes the future perfect: "j'aurai rassemblé". "Aurais" is conditional, "auras" does not match "je", and "avais" is pluperfect. Rule: after quand, an action completed before a future action uses the futur antérieur. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Maman a divisé le gâteau en trois morceaux égaux ; ainsi elle a donné ____ à chacun des trois enfants.
questions.corrige_markdown: Three equal parts means each child gets one third: "un tiers". A quarter, a fifth or three quarters do not correspond to a division into three. Rule: a whole split into 3 equal parts gives thirds. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - numbers and fractions

questions.enonce_markdown: Le lancement des activités de la Semaine Nationale du Bilinguisme ____ dans notre établissement.
questions.corrige_markdown: To say that an event happens, French uses "avoir lieu". The subject is "le lancement", singular, so "a eu lieu". "Ont eu lieu" and "ont pris place" are plural, and "prendre place" means to take a seat, not to take place (it is an English calque). Rule: an event "a lieu"; the verb agrees with its singular subject. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Pour bâtir une nation prospère nous devons tous <u>mettre la main à la pâte</u>. L’expression soulignée signifie :
questions.corrige_markdown: "Mettre la main à la pâte" is a figurative expression meaning to take an active part in a job and help get it done. The literal readings about bread, groundnut paste or stealing dough are traps. Rule: idioms are understood as a whole, not word by word. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Faire la pâte d’arachide avec la main.
Apporter son aide dans la réalisation d’une tâche.

questions.enonce_markdown: La journaliste a clos l’émission après ____ au revoir aux téléspectateurs.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Après" is followed by the past infinitive (an action finished before the closing): auxiliary + past participle. "Dire" takes "avoir", so "après avoir dit au revoir". "S'être dite" and "être dit" use the wrong auxiliary, and "avoir dire" mixes two infinitives. Rule: après + avoir/être + past participle. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Mon père est diabétique, raison ____ il ne consomme pas du sucre.
questions.corrige_markdown: The relative pronoun must express the reason (cause or purpose) and refer to the feminine noun "raison": "raison pour laquelle". "De laquelle" and "à laquelle" take other prepositions that do not suit "consommer" here, and "duquel" is masculine. Rule: la raison pour laquelle = the reason why. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Nos joueurs ont porté des maillots ____ pour le match d’ouverture.
questions.corrige_markdown: A colour word taken from a fruit or a flower (orange) is used as a noun and stays invariable: "des maillots orange". "Oranges" would agree like an ordinary adjective, "orangers" is a tree, and "orangés" (orangey) describes a shade, which is not the colour itself. Rule: nouns used as colours are invariable (orange, marron). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Ce téléphone est ____ performant ____ le mien parce qu’il a plus de fonctions.
questions.corrige_markdown: Having more functions makes this phone better, so the comparative of superiority "plus performant que" is used. "Moins ... que" and "aussi ... que" express inferiority and equality, and "mieux" cannot modify an adjective (it is the comparative of the adverb "bien"). Rule: plus + adjective + que = more ... than. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Qu’il ____, qu’il neige, j’irai au champ.
questions.corrige_markdown: In the fixed structure "que ..., que ..." (whether ... or ...), the verb is in the subjunctive: "qu'il pleuve, qu'il neige". "Pleut" is indicative, "pleure" means cries and "pleuvoir" is the infinitive. Rule: "que + subjunctive" expresses a hypothesis or an alternative. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: J’ai vu un troupeau de bœufs qui ____ l’herbe sur la colline.
questions.corrige_markdown: The relative "qui" refers to the animals that do the grazing, "les bœufs" (plural), so the verb is "broutent". "Broutes" and "broutez" are second person forms. "Broute" (agreement with the collective "troupeau") is possible in a very strict reading, but when the action is done by each animal the plural is the standard choice. Rule: the verb after qui agrees with its antecedent, here the animals that graze. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Si le COVID-19 n’avait pas résurgi, le gouvernement n’____ pas annulé le défilé du 11 février.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Si" + pluperfect ("n'avait pas résurgi") is an unreal condition in the past, so the main clause takes the past conditional: "n'aurait pas annulé", with "le gouvernement" singular. "Auraient" is plural, "avait" would give a pluperfect and "aura" a future. Rule: si + plus-que-parfait, ... conditionnel passé. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: J’ai deux voitures de luxe dans mon parking ; ____ voulez-vous acheter ?
questions.corrige_markdown: The interrogative pronoun replaces "deux voitures", which is feminine plural, so "lesquelles". "Laquelle" is singular, "lequel" masculine singular and "lesquels" masculine plural. Rule: lequel, laquelle, lesquels, lesquelles agree with the noun they stand for. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Le père Noël ____ de jolis cadeaux aux enfants cette année.
questions.corrige_markdown: The sentence needs the passé composé with the third person singular auxiliary: "a distribué". "As" goes with tu, "ont" with a plural subject, and "à distribuer" is a preposition plus infinitive. Rule: passé composé = avoir conjugated + past participle. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Marie lave les habits dans une machine à laver. Elle ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: Washing clothes in a washing machine is "faire la lessive" (do the laundry). "Faire la vaisselle" is washing dishes, "faire la cuisine" is cooking and "faire des courses" is shopping. Rule: faire la lessive = to do the washing. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: ____ est la marque de votre ordinateur ?
questions.corrige_markdown: The interrogative adjective agrees with the noun "marque" (feminine singular): "Quelle est la marque...". "Quel" is masculine, "quels" and "quelles" are plural. Rule: quel agrees in gender and number with its noun, even when separated by the verb être. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Le Ministre a décidé ____ donner des primes aux meilleurs élèves bilingues dans tous les établissements.
questions.corrige_markdown: The verb "décider" takes "de" before an infinitive: "a décidé de donner". "À" would suit "se mettre à", "pour" expresses purpose, and "a" is the verb avoir. Rule: décider de + infinitive. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: J’aime ton habit. Combien ____ as-tu acheté ?
questions.corrige_markdown: The direct object pronoun replaces "ton habit" (masculine singular), and it elides before the vowel of "as": "l'as-tu acheté". "Le" cannot be used before a vowel without elision, "les" is plural and "la" is feminine. Rule: le/la become l' before a vowel or a mute h. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Mon père n’aime pas les chaussures que ma sœur lui ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: With avoir, the past participle agrees with a direct object placed BEFORE the verb. Here "que" stands for "les chaussures" (feminine plural), so the participle is "achetées". "Achetés" is masculine, "acheté" has no agreement and "achetée" is singular. Rule: the object placed before avoir + participle governs the agreement. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Après trois leçons sur la création d’un fichier, je ne comprends toujours ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Je ne comprends toujours rien" means I still understand nothing, which suits the context of three lessons without result. "Jamais" and "plus" clash with "toujours" (still), and "guère" (hardly) does not fit this sentence. Rule: ne ... rien = nothing, with "toujours" meaning still. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: ____ élève est très polie ; elle me salue tout le temps.
questions.corrige_markdown: The pupil is a girl ("polie", "elle"), so the feminine demonstrative adjective "cette" is used even before a vowel. "Cet" is masculine before a vowel, "ce" is masculine before a consonant, and "c'est" is a pronoun with a verb. Rule: cette is the feminine demonstrative, kept before vowels. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: "My daughter is sixteen today". Could be rendered into French as :
questions.corrige_markdown: In French age is expressed with the verb avoir and the noun "ans": "Ma fille a seize ans aujourd'hui". Option A uses the imperfect (past), option B means she has become sixteen years older, and option D forgets "ans". Rule: never use être for age; say "avoir ... ans". **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - translation into French

choix.texte: Ma fille avait seize ans aujourd’hui.
Ma fille a seize ans de plus aujourd’hui.
Ma fille a seize ans aujourd’hui.

questions.enonce_markdown: Tout ____ le repas, maman surveillait le bébé dans son berceau.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Tout en" + present participle (gérondif) expresses two actions at the same time: "tout en préparant". The bare participle "préparant" lacks "en" after "tout", the infinitive "préparer" is wrong and "préparait" is a conjugated verb. Rule: tout en + participe présent = while doing. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Cette photocopieuse est neuve, mais ____ est vieille.
questions.corrige_markdown: The demonstrative pronoun replaces "cette photocopieuse" (feminine singular), so "celle-là". "Celui-là" is masculine singular, "celles-là" feminine plural, "ceux-là" masculine plural. Rule: the demonstrative pronoun agrees with the noun it replaces. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Passage for questions 46 to 50**

M. Ntam était le père géniteur d’Ayuk et Eku. Après les études universitaires, les deux diplômés n’avaient pas trouvé le travail. Ils se sont lancés dans la révolution verte dans leur champ, en se disant qu’un tiens vaut mieux que deux tu l’auras. Après chaque récolte de leurs produits vivriers, ils montaient sur leur moto, et à grande vitesse, se rendaient en ville pour vendre leurs produits afin d’acheter ce dont ils avaient besoin dans la famille.

Who were Ayuk and Eku?
questions.corrige_markdown: The text says M. Ntam was their "père géniteur", which means biological father, so Ayuk and Eku are his biological children. "Legal children" would suit a "père légal" or adoptive father, "genital" is a wrong word (a false friend of "géniteur"), and the graduates are a description of the two sons, not the relation asked. Rule: père géniteur = biological father. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: The legal children of Mr. Ntam.
The genital children of Mr. Ntam.
The university graduates of Mr. Ntam

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 46 to 50 above)

After university studies, they;
questions.corrige_markdown: They did not find a job, so they started the "révolution verte dans leur champ", that is, a green revolution on their own farm: they went into farming. "Se lancer dans" means to launch oneself into, not to throw oneself, and nothing says they threw away their diplomas or refused jobs. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 46 to 50 above)

What were they saying to themselves?
questions.corrige_markdown: "Un tiens vaut mieux que deux tu l'auras" is the French proverb that corresponds exactly to "A bird in hand is worth two in the bush". Options B, C and D only paraphrase or distort the idea (B is close in meaning, but A is the proverb itself and keeps the contrast with "two"; C is a literal mistranslation). **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: A bird in hand is worth two in the bush.
What you have is better than what you are expecting.
Your own is better than the two which you will get.
Hold tight to what you have now.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 46 to 50 above)

What did they do after every harvest
questions.corrige_markdown: After each harvest they got on their motorbike and, "à grande vitesse" (at high speed), went to town to sell their produce, so the best match is "Speed up to town". "Sit on their bikes" only describes the first step of the journey (they mount the bike) and not what they did after the harvest as a whole; nothing in the text says they stayed in town or bought a new bike. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Live in town for a while.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 46 to 50 above)

State their mission in town.
questions.corrige_markdown: The text says they went to town "pour vendre leurs produits afin d'acheter ce dont ils avaient besoin dans la famille": to sell their farm produce and to buy what the family needed. Options A, B and D are not stated, and B is only partial. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Sell their farm produce and buy their family needs.
To miss the village for a while.
